title: notify-orchestrator hook relays the orchestrator's own idle message back as a worker needs-input alert
description: Mirrors opum-agent OPAG-62, observed 2026-09-06 during the fleet restart. Three worker panes (opum-doc, quest-cli, opum-marketplace) sat unprompted in the claude agents view. Each time the orchestrator session finished a turn whose last line asked the user to prompt those panes, a Notification hook fired in a worker's own session and delivered an alert to the orchestrator reading '[auto] opum-doc is waiting: agent_needs_input. opum-agent needs your input: ...' with the orchestrator's own sentence quoted as if it were the worker's question. Six such alerts arrived in a row, none carrying any change in worker state, and every acknowledgement the orchestrator wrote triggered another relay -- a loop. Mechanism (confirmed by a fixture, see below): hooks/notify-orchestrator.sh discriminates idle_prompt by scanning the worker's own transcript for a pending AskUserQuestion, but treats agent_needs_input as unconditionally STUCK with no equivalent check (see the case statement after the idle_prompt block) -- so a notification whose message field happens to originate from the orchestrator's side of a cross-session delivery is relayed verbatim as this worker's own question. The hook shipped under OPAG-32; the fix belongs here since opum-workflow ships from this repo. Investigate: which session's transcript the harness attaches to notification_type agent_needs_input in this shape, why the classification fired on a peer's plain prose rather than a genuine local block, and whether the alert should be suppressed (or requalified) when the quoted message text does not originate from the recipient session's own turn.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The mechanism is recorded on this task: which transcript/notification field the hook reads and why the classification fired on the orchestrator idle message
hooks/test/run-tests.sh carries a fixture test that fails against the current hook for this shape and passes after the fix (added 2026-09-06, currently failing by design)
An orchestrator idle message no longer produces a worker needs-input alert, observed in the fleet after the plugin release

implementationNotes: MECHANISM CONFIRMED 2026-09-06 by fixture (hooks/test/run-tests.sh, 'OMARK-10/OPAG-62' section). Reproduced by feeding notify-orchestrator.sh a synthetic Notification payload {notification_type: agent_needs_input, message: an orchestrator-authored sentence} from a worker cwd (opum-doc) in the fleet allowlist. The idle_prompt branch already discriminates a genuine human-decision block by scanning the worker's own transcript_path for a pending (unanswered) AskUserQuestion tool_use/tool_result pair -- see the block starting 'AskUserQuestion does NOT get its own notification_type' in notify-orchestrator.sh. agent_needs_input has no equivalent discriminator: it falls straight into the STUCK case (idle_prompt|human_decision|permission_prompt|agent_needs_input|elicitation_dialog|elicitation_url_dialog|unknown) and is relayed via herdr agent prompt using whatever the payload's message/title/body field contains, unchecked for whose turn produced it. Root cause is therefore an asymmetry: idle_prompt is requalified against the worker's OWN transcript before alerting; agent_needs_input is not requalified against anything, so a cross-session delivery landing in the worker's session (whose message field is authored by the sender, i.e. the orchestrator) is indistinguishable from the worker genuinely blocking. Fix direction not yet chosen -- needs to establish what distinguishes a genuine local agent_needs_input from one produced by inbound cross-session delivery (harness field TBD, since the Notification schema is unpublished per this hook's own comments) before writing the fix. Fixture is a hard gate: it fails today (unfixed) and must pass once corrected.

Root cause confirmed empirically, not just fixture-reproduced: analyzed hooks/notify-orchestrator.sh's own audit log (~/.local/state/opum-fleet/orchestrator-notifications.jsonl, 305 entries, 2026-08-31 through 2026-09-07). All 64 agent_needs_input entries carry a message of the shape '<name> needs your input: ...' where <name> is NEVER the receiving worker's own repo -- 54/64 name the orchestrator ('opum-agent'), the remainder name other sessions ('opum-handoff ...', 'exit command handling'). Zero of 64 self-name. Fix: requalify agent_needs_input the same way idle_prompt already is -- if the message matches that pattern and the named session isn't this repo, reclassify to a new 'foreign_needs_input' kind that routes to quiet (exit 0), same bucket as idle_prompt. A message that doesn't match the pattern falls through unchanged, still STUCK -- preserves the hook's existing bias toward a spurious alert over a missed one for genuinely unrecognized shapes.

Verified against a real captured payload (not just the synthetic fixture): fed the first real agent_needs_input entry from the audit log through the fixed hook in a sandbox and confirmed it's suppressed. Added a companion positive test (hooks/test/run-tests.sh) proving a message that does NOT match the relay pattern still alerts -- the fix must not over-suppress. Full suite: 41/41 passing (was 40/40 before this task's fixture, which itself failed by design until now).
finalSummary: Fixed in hooks/notify-orchestrator.sh: agent_needs_input is now requalified the same way idle_prompt already was. Root cause confirmed against 305 real logged notifications, not just the fixture -- 64/64 real agent_needs_input entries carried a message naming a DIFFERENT session ('<name> needs your input: ...'), never this worker's own repo, confirming a 100% consistent cross-session misattribution rather than a genuine local block. Fix reclassifies a matching-but-foreign-named message to a new foreign_needs_input kind, routed to quiet -- same bucket as idle_prompt. A message that doesn't match the pattern still alerts, preserving the hook's bias toward a spurious alert over a missed one. 41/41 tests pass (fixture + a new companion positive test proving no over-suppression). Criterion 2 (observed in the fleet after release) can't be checked until the plugin actually ships this fix.
